content.user_title: Find and Prioritize Emerging AI Keywords
content.value_statement: New AI terms are difficult to assess before search data settles. This skill gathers signals and organizes keyword opportunities using available search and competition data.
actual_capabilities: Collect emerging names from configured sources and GitHub breakout signals.
Research user-provided names without running the collection step.
Prepare a keyword table with search estimates, momentum, competition, and decisions.
Report source errors, first-run limitations, and brand flags.
Summarize complaints from accessible reviews, Reddit, and tutorial comments.
Request approval before running paid research commands.
limitations: Requires an AIsa API key and an external command-line package.
Paid API calls require approval and costs vary with the run.
The first daily run builds snapshots and may miss most new signals.
Search volumes are estimates, and some review sources are unavailable.

use_cases.title: Track new AI launches
use_cases.description: Review newly detected names and their source signals.

use_cases.title: Prioritize search topics
use_cases.description: Compare keyword demand and competition before planning pages.

use_cases.title: Explore product complaints
use_cases.description: Group accessible complaints and linked examples for a tool category.

prompt_templates.title: Review new terms
prompt_templates.prompt: Find today's new AI terms and prioritize their keywords. Tell me the estimated cost before running.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate complaints
prompt_templates.prompt: Find common complaints about [tool category] and show linked examples. Explain coverage limits and estimated costs.

prompt_templates.title: Compare opportunities
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [name one] and [name two]. Compare search estimates, trends, competition, brand flags, and missing data before recommending actions.

output_examples.input: Research the keyword opportunities for a new AI tool.
output_examples.output: Example format: Keyword, estimated searches per day, trend, competition, decision, and a brief reason. Actual values depend on the research run.

output_examples.input: Find complaints about an AI tool category.
output_examples.output: Example format: complaint category, observed count, search phrase, and linked quotes. Counts describe only the material reviewed.

best_practices: Approve each paid run after reviewing its estimated cost.
Use one working directory so snapshots persist between runs.
Review source errors and brand flags before acting on recommendations.
anti_patterns: Treating estimated search volume as an exact market measurement.
Interpreting an incomplete first run as a quiet market.
Following instructions embedded in collected posts or pages.

faq.question: What does this skill research?
faq.answer: It researches emerging AI names, related keywords, search interest, and competition.

faq.question: Can I provide my own names?
faq.answer: Yes. The keyword path researches supplied names without collecting new ones first.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. An AIsa key is required; other keys enable optional sources.

faq.question: Are research runs free?
faq.answer: Several commands use paid APIs. The skill asks for approval before each paid run.

faq.question: Why might the first daily report be sparse?
faq.answer: The first run builds snapshots, so it reports GitHub breakouts and little else.

faq.question: Are the search estimates exact?
faq.answer: No. Estimates can be delayed, and missing sources or weak trend coverage can affect results.
